Energy transition

Paradise

There is plenty of sun and wind. There is also an imported-oil bill, and no neighboring grid to call when local supply falls short.

Play Paradise↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Free to play in your browser. Choose your difficulty in the game.

Location
Honolulu, Hawaii
Starts in
2003
Your term
13 years

The situation

Your starting point

Take over an island utility in 2003 with oil, wind and solar generation. The oil plant provides much of your capacity, leaving the utility exposed when fuel prices rise.

You can build more local clean power, but the island has to balance its own supply. Good annual production is not enough if the fleet cannot cover a quiet evening or a stretch of weak wind.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Reduce dependence on imported fuel

    Compare the upfront cost of new generation with years of oil purchases. Watch how fuel prices change the value of your investments.

  2. 02

    Plan for gaps between renewables

    Give storage and backup a job in your fleet. Their value becomes clearer in the hours when sun and wind do not meet demand.

  3. 03

    Keep an island's margin for error

    Build enough flexibility to handle changing demand without relying on imports. Every shortage has to be solved on your side of the ocean.

Put your plan to the test

How much of the island's imported oil can you replace without leaving a gap in supply?

Build, watch what happens, and try a different approach. The grid is yours to run.
